input.summary: parts/chimneys.mjs builds the 8 house stacks (plots 0-4 and 7, twin and two-stack plots included) with brick footings, 8 hearth faces, 8 stoves and the plot 6 bread oven with its own stack; make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with this part at 200 blocks and no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes. Fit reports no chimney faults.
left: Stoves at (4,3,15), (7,3,15), (41,3,15), (52,3,15), (87,3,15), (92,3,15) stand directly in front of their hearth mouths, so the mouth is blocked. Kept the plan's ROOMS coordinates; the room designer may move each stove one cell into the room (e.g. to z14) so the fire shows.

Roof-to-stack check not done: roofs.mjs is still a stub in this copy (no roof.json), so the roof must be cut back round each stack and the mouths 1-2 courses above the roof verified after the roof lands.

Hearth surrounds (hearth_face stone_bricks) orphan where the back wall is missing: (50,3,16), (86,3,16), (93,3,16) dangle because shell_b is still a stub in this copy (0 placed). They should resolve when shell B lands.
Deepslate band and corbelled courses on the stacks rely on chimney()'s defaults; not inspected at block level.
Bread oven mouth and vault are built from bread_oven; the oven stack flue cells (75,3..4,16) are forced to air after the vault, not by the helper.

waste.what: Worked out each stack footprint, flue column, fire cell and footing by hand from plan.md's RESERVED table and the FACADES text, then typed each coordinate into the part.
waste.cost: about 10 coordinate sets, 8 chimney calls and 8 footing boxes written out by hand
waste.tool: A data table in plan.md (or a RESERVED-to-JSON export) that a part can import, so the chimney part reads each mouth, top and footprint instead of retyping them.

waste.what: Footing fills under each stack (y1..2 bricks where air) so the stack rests on the ground, found only after the structure check reported floating groups.
waste.cost: one failed build cycle; a fix loop of make, check, fit
waste.tool: chimney_stack / chimney() should lay its own footing at the stand level (y1) when the footprint is air, and say so in its result.

waste.what: Forced the bread oven's flue cells (75,3..4,16) to air after bread_oven(), because the vault's brick_slab crown walled the flue (fit: 'roof's brick_slab walls the flue at y 4').
waste.cost: one fit fault traced and one manual set() pair
waste.tool: bread_oven() should leave its flue cell (x+2, y+3..y+4, z+2) air by construction, as its own comment already says it does for y+3.

waste.what: Diagnosed a 'refused writes into earlier parts' failure on the hearth mouths and lintels, which turned out to be the shell's walls in an older copy; re-running make.sh after shell_a changed cleared it.
waste.cost: one make and one check cycle
waste.tool: A report line that names which earlier part owns the refused cell, so the fix goes to the owning worker at once.

waste.what: Per-stack verification by eye: rendered and zoomed twice to read the stacks, because the back elevation at 300 px is too small to see the flues.
waste.tool: mcd render --closeups or a stack-only tile per plot in the card, sized so a 1-wide flue reads.

companions.task: Lay the stack masonry, footings and the bread oven's vault and crown, with the flue cells walled and the deepslate band set; check the courses are constant width through the roof.
Cut the roof's stairs and slabs back round each stack after the roof lands, and confirm the mouths sit 1-2 courses above the roof surface.
Decide the stove and hearth lighting so the stove in front of each back mouth does not hide the fire, and check light at the hearth cells.
